patients.summary: Man with HIV since 2010 and intermittent ART adherence, followed by an outside ID clinic, living in transitional housing and working construction on and off. Over 2020-2026 he has oral hairy leukoplakia, candidal esophagitis, AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma, a second PJP pneumonia, primary CNS lymphoma presenting with a seizure, and cryptosporidiosis after the practice last saw him.

documents.title: New Patient Intake Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller is looking for a primary care doctor in town. Has not had one for a while; gets his HIV care at an outside infectious disease clinic and wants a PCP for everything else. Insurance is MassHealth/Medicaid, card verified. Mailing address is a transitional housing program on Pleasant St. Cell is the best number, ok to leave a message.

Scheduled new patient visit 7/16 at 9:00. Release of information signed for the ID clinic and his last primary care office; requests faxed today. Asked him to bring all his medication bottles.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, high MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

36M here to set up primary care. HIV since 2010, care at an outside ID clinic, which he says he goes to "most of the time." Admits there have been stretches over the years when he stopped his pills, usually when things got chaotic with housing. Currently taking his once-daily ART pill and the TMP-SMX three days a week. Had PJP pneumonia last year (2018) when he was off meds, hospitalized, recovered. Has had thrush in the past and keeps fluconazole on hand for it. No current mouth symptoms.

Substance use: cocaine and meth, both snorted and smoked, on and off for years. Used a few weeks ago. Not in a program. Open to talking about it, not ready to commit to anything today.

Social: lives in a transitional housing program here in Easthampton, shared kitchen. Works construction when there's work. Quit cigarettes in 2017, about 10 pack-years. Drinks once or twice a month. Single.

PMH: HIV; PJP 2018; oral thrush in past; polysubstance use.
PSH: tonsillectomy at 12.
Meds (all from ID): bictegravir/FTC/TAF 1 tab daily; TMP-SMX DS 1 tab M/W/F; fluconazole 100 mg daily prn thrush; acetaminophen 500 mg prn.
Allergies: none known to medications.
FH: dad has high blood pressure, mom type 2 diabetes. No blood cancers or immune problems in the family that he knows of.

ROS: no fevers, sweats, cough, weight change, diarrhea, rash. Mood ok. PHQ-2 1.

Exam: thin-normal build, comfortable. Oropharynx clear, no plaques or thrush. No cervical/axillary nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without lesions. No edema. Alert, appropriate.

A/P
1. HIV - ID manages ART and prophylaxis; will get their notes. Adherence reinforced; he knows what happens when he stops.
2. Polysubstance use (cocaine/methamphetamine) - discussed harm reduction, never use alone, offered referral to outpatient treatment; he'll think about it.
3. Housing - transitional program; gave info for the housing navigator at the community action agency.
4. Hx PJP, hx thrush - on prophylaxis per ID.
5. Health maintenance - Tdap given today. CMP, CBC, lipids drawn. Flu shot in the fall.

RTC 3-4 months. Records request, prior primary care and ID clinic.

documents.title: Your recent lab work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Timothy, your blood work from Tuesday came back fine: kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal, cholesterol in a good range. Nothing to change. See you in the fall.

documents.title: Records Received - Prior Primary Care Office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Two pages faxed back from his former primary care office in response to our July request: an old medication list (same ART, TMP-SMX and fluconazole he takes now) and an immunization printout without dates for the last several years. No visit notes; the office said he had not been seen there in a few years. Nothing yet from the ID clinic; second request faxed. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Walk-in for flu vaccine. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, VIS reviewed. Tolerated, no reaction during 15 minute observation. Reminded of his follow-up in November.

documents.title: No-Show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient did not arrive for 10:30 follow-up. Called cell, mailbox full. Text sent with our number to rebook.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Missed November, came in today after our text. Says work dried up for the winter and he's been around the house more, which is not always good for him. Has used cocaine a couple of times since we met, meth once. No overdoses, nobody hurt. Still on the waitlist for a permanent unit through the housing program.

Taking ART daily "pretty much"; last ID visit in the summer, next one in the new year. Taking the TMP-SMX. No mouth sores, fevers, cough or weight change.

PHQ-9 4. Sleep a bit off.

Exam: NAD. Mouth clear. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema. Skin clear.

A/P
1. Polysubstance use - still intermittent use. Motivational conversation; he says he'd like to be done with it "eventually." Gave walk-in hours for the outpatient recovery program; naloxone discussed, he already carries some from the housing program.
2. HIV - per ID. Asked him to sign another release so their notes reach us.
3. Housing - waitlisted, no change.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Routine in-person visits on hold for the next several weeks because of COVID. Spoke with patient, cancelled tomorrow's visit. He has no urgent issues. Will offer a video or phone visit when the schedule opens.

documents.title: Refill Request - TMP-SMX
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed refill request for TMP-SMX DS. Prescriber on file is his ID clinic. Called the ID clinic nurse line, they will send it today. Let patient know; he has 2 tablets left, enough until pickup.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, he is in his room at the housing program; consent for video visit obtained.

He says the lockdown months were rough. Used cocaine and some meth earlier this month, a few days in a row, and it scared him how fast it took over. Wants to stop for real this time. No chest pain, no seizures, no injection use.

Taking ART and TMP-SMX. Had a phone visit with ID last month.

Mood: down but not hopeless, no thoughts of harming himself. Eating ok.

A/P
1. Polysubstance use (cocaine/methamphetamine) - motivated today. Warm handoff: messaged the outpatient recovery program, they will call him this week for intake (telehealth groups running). Carries naloxone. Talked through triggers (no work, isolation) and who he can call.
2. HIV - continue per ID.
Video check-in in 3 months, sooner if he wants.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, at home.

No cocaine or meth since June. Went to the recovery program's online groups through the summer, now goes once a week. Picked up some framing work in August. Housing unchanged.

Taking ART daily, TMP-SMX MWF. Has an ID visit in December. No thrush lately.

A/P
1. Polysubstance use - about 3 months without use. Strongly encouraged; keep groups going.
2. HIV - ID in December.
3. Flu shot next month at a nurse visit.
RTC early next year in person if allowed.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Masked, screened at door, afebrile. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated without issue.

conditions.label: HIV-related opportunistic skin infection
conditions.note: Recent infection reported by patient, healed by the ID visit; per ID problem list

documents.title: Infectious Diseases Clinic Letter
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASES CLINIC - VISIT SUMMARY TO PRIMARY CARE
Date of visit: 12/17/2020

Scheduled HIV follow-up. Feels well today, nothing new. Reports he is taking his ART every day. Most recent CD4 before today was 350 in June. Mentions a skin infection earlier this fall that has cleared; we have added HIV-related opportunistic skin infection to his problem list. He asked whether he is due for any vaccines.

Current: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily; TMP-SMX DS three times weekly; fluconazole 100 mg daily prn thrush; acetaminophen prn. NKDA.
Social: one sexual partner, uses condoms every time. Former smoker. No drug use for about 6 months.

Exam: well appearing. Unremarkable exam today, including skin and oropharynx.

Results today: CD4 220 cells/mm3. HIV-1 RNA undetectable. VZV IgG negative.

Impression: HIV, virally suppressed on current regimen; CD4 lower than in June. Not immune to varicella.

Plan: continue current regimen and prophylaxis. He is seronegative for VZV with a CD4 above 200; we would support varicella vaccination (2 doses, 3 months apart) through his primary care office if convenient for him. Return in 6 months with labs.

documents.title: ID Letter Follow-up - Varicella Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PCP reviewed ID letter (CD4 220, undetectable viral load, VZV IgG negative) and agrees with varicella vaccine x2. Called patient, explained it is a live vaccine and ok at his CD4 per ID. He wants it. Nurse visit booked 1/12. Vaccine ordered from distributor.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Varicella Vaccine Dose 1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for first varicella dose per PCP order (VZV IgG negative on ID labs 12/17, CD4 220). Denies fever or new illness today. No other live vaccines in the past 4 weeks. Varicella vaccine 0.5 mL subcut left upper arm, VIS given. Told him a mild rash or sore arm can happen within a few weeks; call if a rash shows up. Dose 2 due in 3 months - booked 4/13.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Varicella Vaccine Dose 2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second varicella dose. No reaction after dose 1 other than a sore arm for a day. Feeling well. Got his second COVID shot a few days ago at a community vaccine site; no issue spacing these per protocol. Varicella 0.5 mL subcut right upper arm. Series complete.

documents.title: COVID-19 Vaccine Record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Patient brought in his CDC card. Moderna dose 1 on 3/18/21 and dose 2 on 4/16/21 at the county vaccination clinic. Entered into immunization history; copy scanned.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Feels good. One year almost without cocaine or meth (last use June 2020); still checks in with his recovery group most weeks. Working steadily on a roofing crew this spring. Still in the transitional program, moved up on the list.

HIV: ID follows, says his last labs there were "good." Takes ART daily, TMP-SMX MWF. Has not needed the fluconazole this year. Both varicella doses done, COVID series done.

ROS negative: no fevers, sweats, cough, mouth sores, diarrhea, rashes, weight change. PHQ-9 2.

Exam: well. HEENT normal, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, no HSM. Skin: no lesions. Ext: no edema. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance - CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c today (on INSTI-based ART, dad with HTN, mom with T2DM). Tdap 2019, flu yearly, COVID done, varicella series done.
2. HIV - per ID.
3. Polysubstance use disorder - no use in a year. Keep doing what he's doing.
RTC 6 months or prn.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Timothy - labs from your physical look good. Sugar (A1c) normal, cholesterol fine, kidney and liver normal, blood counts normal. Recheck next year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Tongue Lesion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Noticed a white patch on the right side of his tongue about a week ago. Doesn't hurt. Tried his fluconazole for 3 days thinking it was thrush, no change. Also says he's been more tired on and off and his work pants are looser - not trying to lose weight. Hasn't been to ID since the spring; admits he's missed some ART doses this summer.

Exam: weight down a little from June. Oropharynx: whitish patch along the right lateral tongue with a ridged surface; does not come off with a tongue blade. No other oral lesions. No cervical nodes. Lungs clear, heart regular.

A/P
1. Tongue lesion, not removable, no response to fluconazole - not typical thrush. Referral to ENT for evaluation; front desk to request a near-term slot.
2. Fatigue, some weight loss, missed doses - asked him to call ID this week for labs. He agrees.
RTC after ENT.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consult Letter
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OTOLARYNGOLOGY - CONSULT LETTER
Visit date: 09/01/2021

Thank you for sending this 38-year-old man with HIV. Two weeks of a white area on the side of the tongue, no pain. Some fatigue on and off and weight loss over the last several months. Patient reports more than one current sexual partner and past recreational drug use.

On exam the lesion on the lateral tongue border is corrugated and firmly attached and does not scrape away. No cervical adenopathy.

Impression: oral hairy leukoplakia.

Recommendations: no local treatment needed. It reflects his immune status, so the key step is follow-up with his HIV clinic for viral load, CD4 count and adherence. Happy to see him again if it changes in character.

documents.title: ENT Letter Reviewed
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PCP reviewed ENT letter - oral hairy leukoplakia, no treatment, needs ID follow-up. Called patient. He says he has an ID appointment "in a couple weeks" but didn't know the date. Gave him the ID clinic number again and asked him to confirm it today.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid after work. No contraindications. Asked about COVID booster - plans to get one at the pharmacy next month.

documents.title: COVID-19 Booster Record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: State immunization registry shows Moderna booster given 11/19/21 at a community pharmacy. Added to immunization history.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Tongue plaques still there, now on both sides. Not painful. Bothered by how they look and the texture. He did see ID in the fall; they told him to stick with his ART. He says he's taking it "most days." Weight back up a bit over the holidays. No fevers.

Exam: corrugated white plaques along both lateral tongue borders, unchanged character, do not scrape. No other oral lesions. No nodes. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Oral hairy leukoplakia - persistent. He'd like another opinion about whether anything can be done for the appearance; referral to dermatology (they see oral mucosal lesions). Wait list is long.
2. HIV - adherence again. ID follow-up.
3. Polysubstance use disorder - still no use.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Referral Authorization - Dermatology
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dermatology office called; MassHealth referral number needed before they can book. Entered referral in the payer portal, number faxed to them. They offered 5/2 at 1:30. Patient notified by text and confirmed.

events.reason: Fatigue, fever, weight loss; oral plaques

documents.title: Dermatology Consult Letter
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY - CONSULT LETTER
Visit date: 05/02/2022

Referred for oral plaques. At the visit his bigger concern was feeling unwell for about two months: tired, fevers off and on, and about 10 kg of weight loss he did not intend. No cough, no diarrhea, no night sweats. Sexually active with more than one partner, does not always use protection. No known drug allergies.

Vitals: T 38.2 C, BP 120/75, HR 88, BMI 21.

Exam: several white, corrugated plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be wiped off; no other oral lesions. Skin and remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs drawn here: CD4 180 cells/uL. RPR non-reactive. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative. Hepatitis C antibody negative.

Impression: oral hairy leukoplakia, consistent with the ENT assessment; no dermatologic treatment indicated. The constitutional symptoms and falling CD4 are the more pressing issue and need prompt review by his HIV physician; patient told this directly today. Copy to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after dermatology. Down about 10 kg since February. Tired, fevers on and off. Honest that he's been missing a lot of ART doses since winter - says the pill bottle "gets lost" when he's moving between rooms in the program. No drug use. Eating less, no diarrhea, no cough.

Derm letter reviewed: CD4 180, RPR nonreactive, hep B sAg and hep C Ab negative.

Exam: thin. Afebrile here today. Tongue plaques unchanged. No thrush. No nodes. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no HSM. Skin clear.

A/P
1. HIV with falling CD4, missed doses, weight loss and fevers - needs ID now, not in the fall. Called the ID clinic from the room with him; they will see him next month and draw viral load. Pill organizer given; set a phone alarm together.
2. Weight loss - follow weight. Return in 3 months, sooner if fevers worsen, cough or diarrhea.
3. Oral hairy leukoplakia - unchanged.

documents.title: Follow-up Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check whether he made his ID appointment. He went last week, says they "went over everything" and he is back to taking the pill every day with the organizer. No fevers this week. Eating better. Reminded him of August visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels better than spring. Fevers stopped. Up 2 kg. Taking ART with the organizer, misses maybe one dose a week. Saw ID in June.

Exam: thin but looks better. Tongue plaques still present, smaller. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. HIV - improving adherence; ID follow-up continues.
2. Weight - slowly recovering.
3. Pneumococcal vaccine - indicated with HIV; PCV20 given today, no further pneumococcal doses needed.
4. Flu and COVID bivalent at a nurse visit in October.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine IM left deltoid and Pfizer bivalent COVID booster IM right deltoid. Screening negative. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: No-Show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No show for 10:00. Number goes straight to voicemail. Left message and sent a portal note to rebook.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: sorry i missed in december my phone was off for a while. can i come in sometime in feb. mornings better

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No problem, Timothy. You're booked Tuesday 2/21 at 9:20. Reply here if that doesn't work.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: dysphagia and odynophagia in advanced HIV

documents.title: Office Visit - Dysphagia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About a week of food hanging up behind the breastbone, and it hurts to swallow. Liquids go down better than solids. White patches in his mouth again, a little sore. He stopped his ART sometime in the fall - "I just stopped picking it up" - and has not been back to ID since last summer. Still taking TMP-SMX some weeks. No drug use. No vomiting, no blood, no black stools.

Exam: thin. Oral thrush on the buccal mucosa and palate, plus the old tongue plaques. No nodes. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Dysphagia/odynophagia with thrush, off ART - concern for esophageal infection. Urgent GI referral; GI office reached by phone and can scope him Monday 2/27.
2. HIV off ART - he agrees to call ID; given the number again.
Follow up after GI.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 21 days

reports.text: Specimen: esophagus, mid and distal, biopsies. Gross: four tan mucosal fragments, 0.2 to 0.4 cm, entirely submitted. Microscopic: squamous mucosa with acute inflammation and surface fibrinopurulent debris. Yeast forms and pseudohyphae are present within the debris and invade the squamous epithelium, highlighted on PAS-D stain. No viral cytopathic changes. No dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Esophagus, biopsies: fungal (candidal) esophagitis. Negative for viral cytopathic effect and dysplasia.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consult and Procedure Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CONSULT AND ENDOSCOPY
Date of service: 02/27/2023

History: two weeks of odynophagia and dysphagia with a feeling that food lodges in the mid-chest. New mildly sore white patches in the mouth. Longstanding HIV, prior oral hairy leukoplakia; he acknowledges he has not been taking his antiretrovirals and his HIV has not been controlled.

T 37.8 C (100 F), BP 125/78, HR 88, RR 16. Oral thrush present.

Labs today: CD4 50 cells/mm3. HIV-1 viral load 120,000 copies/mL. CBC and BMP unremarkable.

EGD: linear yellow-white plaques running along the esophagus. Biopsies taken. Stomach and duodenum normal.

Pathology (resulted 3/2): candidal esophagitis; no viral changes, no dysplasia.

Assessment: candidal esophagitis and oropharyngeal candidiasis in a patient with advanced HIV off therapy; medication nonadherence.

Plan: fluconazole 200 mg daily for 21 days, prescription sent. He must re-engage with his HIV clinic to restart ART; we stressed this. GI follow-up only if symptoms persist after treatment.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks into fluconazole from GI. Swallowing much better, mouth less sore. GI letter and path reviewed: candidal esophagitis, CD4 50, viral load 120,000.

We talked plainly about what the CD4 means. He says he stopped ART because he was "tired of being sick about being sick." Not using drugs. Housing the same.

Exam: few residual white patches on palate. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Candidal esophagitis / oral thrush - improving; finish the 21 days.
2. HIV, CD4 50, off ART; medication nonadherence - new ID referral placed and faxed so the clinic reaches out to him; he agrees to go. TMP-SMX: asked him to take it every Mon/Wed/Fri without fail.
RTC 4 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished the fluconazole. Swallowing normal. Mouth not sore.

ID: the clinic left him two messages; he has not called back yet. Said he would this week.

Exam: oropharynx without thrush; leukoplakia plaques on tongue as before. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Candidal esophagitis and thrush - resolved.
2. HIV off ART - pressed again on ID. Gave him the direct scheduling line.
Physical in June.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

Weight up a couple of kg since April. Swallowing fine. Working a few days a week with a siding crew. Three years now without cocaine or meth.

HIV: still has not made it to ID. Says he "keeps meaning to." Not on ART. Taking TMP-SMX most weeks.

ROS: no fever, cough, diarrhea, mouth pain, rash. PHQ-9 3.

Exam: thin. Oropharynx without thrush; tongue plaques persist. No nodes. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft, no HSM. Skin without lesions. No edema.

A/P
1. Health maintenance - CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c. Flu and updated COVID in the fall. Colon screening starts at 45.
2. HIV off ART - another long talk. I re-sent the ID referral with a note asking them to call him directly.
3. Polysubstance use disorder - sustained abstinence.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Timothy - your labs came back without anything worrying: kidneys, liver, sugar and cholesterol are all fine and the blood count is ok. The most important number for you is one we didn't check here, your CD4, which the ID clinic needs to follow. Please call them.

documents.title: Refill Request - Fluconazole
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient called for fluconazole 100 mg refill, has a little thrush. Prescription on file from ID has expired and ID has not seen him this year. PCP authorized one fill of the same prn prescription. Reminded him again to call ID; he says he will.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu IM left deltoid, updated Pfizer COVID IM right deltoid. Afebrile, no acute complaints. Tolerated well.

events.reason: Purple spots on legs and mouth

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: violaceous skin and palatal lesions, advanced HIV

documents.title: Office Visit - Skin and Palate Lesions
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in because of purple spots on both shins that showed up over the last few weeks, and his housemate noticed a purple area on the roof of his mouth. Not painful, not itchy. More tired. Lost about 5 kg since the fall without trying. Not on ART. Has not gone to ID.

Exam: thin. Several violaceous patches and plaques on both lower legs, non-tender. Violaceous patch on the hard palate. No nodes. Abd soft.

A/P
1. Violaceous skin and palatal lesions in advanced HIV off ART - strongly suspect Kaposi sarcoma. Oncology referral placed; they can see him 1/3. Explained what we're worried about.
2. HIV off ART - the most important treatment for this is restarting ART; called ID with him, earliest new-return slot is mid-January, he took it.
3. Weight loss.
RTC after oncology.

conditions.label: Kaposi sarcoma (AIDS-related)
conditions.note: Lower legs and hard palate; biopsy confirmed

documents.title: Oncology Consult Letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ONCOLOGY - CONSULT LETTER
Visit 01/03/2024

Re: 41M with HIV, prior PJP and prior candidal esophagitis, seen for skin lesions. Several weeks of fatigue; painless violaceous patches and plaques on the lower legs and roof of mouth; 5 kg down over 2 months; some early satiety. No fevers, sweats or cough. Has not seen his ID physician in over a year. Takes his antiretrovirals inconsistently and currently is not taking any prophylactic antibiotic.

Exam: thin, pale. Multiple non-blanching violaceous plaques on both lower legs and on the hard palate. No lymphadenopathy. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly.

Hgb 11 g/dL.

Punch biopsy of a left shin plaque taken today; pathology: Kaposi sarcoma, HHV-8 (LANA) positive.

Assessment: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma, skin and palate.

Plan: the first-line treatment is effective ART, which he needs to restart with ID now (appointment this month); restart TMP-SMX prophylaxis. We will follow the lesions with photographs every 3 months. Systemic chemotherapy only if lesions progress despite ART.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Oncology letter reviewed: biopsy confirmed Kaposi sarcoma; plan is ART first, chemo only if it progresses.

He went to ID on 1/18 - first time in well over a year. Restarted the same once-daily ART pill and the TMP-SMX MWF. Says he has taken it every day since, organizer in use. Oncology will see him every 3 months.

Exam: thin. Violaceous plaques on both shins and palate, similar to December. Healed biopsy site left shin. No thrush. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Kaposi sarcoma, AIDS-related - per oncology; ART is the treatment.
2. HIV - back on ART and prophylaxis. Big step; told him so.
3. Anemia on oncology labs (Hgb 11) - CBC and CMP today.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Timothy, your blood count is still a little low (hemoglobin about 11), about the same as at oncology. Kidneys and liver are fine, which matters now that you're back on your HIV medicine. We'll recheck in a few months.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his room. Says he is mostly taking ART, "maybe five or six days a week." TMP-SMX some weeks, not every week. Oncology saw him in April, photographed the spots, no change. Energy a little better. No cough, fever, mouth pain.

A/P
1. HIV - partial adherence; went through what's getting in the way (irregular work hours, sleeping at a friend's some nights). Suggested a second pill organizer to keep at the friend's place.
2. Kaposi sarcoma - stable per patient; oncology following.
Physical in June.

documents.title: No-Show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Did not come for physical. Voicemail left. Will try to rebook in the fall.

results.test: Oxygen partial pressure in arterial blood

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL ED - PHYSICIAN NOTE (abbreviated copy sent to PCP)
Arrival 8/22/2024 19:40

CC: short of breath.

41M with HIV, inconsistent ART, prior PJP and Kaposi sarcoma, brought in by his roommate. Ten days of increasing breathlessness, dry cough and low fevers, more and more tired; now gets winded on stairs or walking a short way. Roommate says he has lost a lot of weight over about 3 months and has had white patches on his tongue at times. No sputum, chest pain or blood in sputum.

Exam: thin, mildly tachypneic. SpO2 89% RA. Thrush. Faint crackles both lungs.

WBC 4.3. CD4 62. HIV-1 RNA >500,000 copies/mL. ABG on room air: PaO2 63 mmHg.
CXR (portable): bilateral diffuse interstitial opacities; no effusion, no pneumothorax.

Impression: presumed Pneumocystis pneumonia with hypoxemia; oral candidiasis; advanced HIV.

Disposition: admitted to medicine on oxygen. TMP-SMX treatment dosing and steroids started in the ED (PaO2 under 70).

medications.drug: sulfamethoxazole 800 MG / trimethoprim 160 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth three times daily to complete 21 days total, then resume 1 tablet three times weekly
40 mg twice daily days 1-5, 40 mg daily days 6-10, 20 mg daily days 11-21 (started in hospital 8/22)
medications.reason: PJP pneumonia with hypoxemia; hospital prescriber

documents.title: Pharmacy Fill History
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Medication fill history pulled after patient called about a hospital stay. Filled 8/30/24: TMP-SMX DS #36 (2 tabs three times a day), prednisone 20 mg taper, bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide #30. Prescriber is a hospitalist at the regional hospital. No discharge summary received; request faxed to medical records.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient called. Discharged Friday 8/30 after about a week in the hospital for pneumonia, "the same kind as before." Breathing better, walking around the house ok, no fever. Taking the big TMP-SMX doses and prednisone. Booked post-hospital visit Thursday 9/5. Fill history pulled (see pharmacy note).

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT

Admitted 8/22 to 8/30 at the regional hospital. Our records: short ED note and the pharmacy fill history; discharge summary requested, not yet received. From Timothy: he was on oxygen for several days, they did a sputum test after a breathing treatment and told him it was PJP again. Treated with high-dose TMP-SMX and a prednisone taper; both run through 9/11, then back to one TMP-SMX DS three times a week. The hospital restarted his HIV pill before he left. ID visit set for October.

Now: breathing much better, mild cough, no fever. Walking to the store without stopping. Appetite poor, weight 59 kg. Mouth no longer sore.

Meds reconciled with his bottles: bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily; TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs TID (through 9/11) then DS MWF; prednisone taper (through 9/11); fluconazole prn; acetaminophen prn.

Exam: thin, no distress. Speaks full sentences. Oropharynx clear. Lungs with a few faint basilar crackles, no wheeze. Heart regular.

A/P
1. PJP pneumonia, recovering - finish treatment course and taper exactly as written, then back to prophylaxis dose. Return precautions reviewed.
2. HIV - ART restarted inpatient; ID in October.
3. Weight loss - calorie-dense foods; housing program kitchen has supplements.
RTC 3-4 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished the high-dose TMP-SMX and the prednisone on 9/11. Back on TMP-SMX DS MWF and says he takes it. Breathing back to normal, no cough. Weight up 2 kg.

He tells me he stopped the HIV pill about a week after he got home - it made him feel sick and he "couldn't do it" on top of the other pills. Has the October ID appointment and says he'll tell them.

Exam: oropharynx clear. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. PJP pneumonia - treated, resolved. Thrush resolved.
2. HIV off ART again (side effects). Told him plainly this is how he ended up in the hospital, twice. Asked him to bring the side effects to ID rather than stopping - there may be things they can adjust. Kept ART on his list; ID prescribes.
3. TMP-SMX prophylaxis - continue; CMP and CBC today after the high-dose course.
4. Flu vaccine today.
RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Labs after the pneumonia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and kidney function are normal after the strong TMP-SMX course - good. Hemoglobin still around 11, about where it was. Keep taking the 3-times-a-week tablet. And please keep the ID appointment this month.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video. Missed the October ID visit (was working a job out of town that week), rebooked for February. Still not taking ART. Takes TMP-SMX MWF. Breathing fine. Oncology saw him in November, spots "the same." Still in the transitional program; new roommate.

A/P
1. HIV off ART - he knows the risk; not ready to restart until he talks to ID about the side effects. Asked him to keep February.
2. Prophylaxis - continue.
In person in February.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels ok. Weight slowly coming up. Saw ID last week; they talked through options, he said he'd "think about it" and did not restart. Taking TMP-SMX MWF faithfully - "that one I don't mess with after last summer." No cough, fever, swallowing trouble.

Exam: thin. Violaceous plaques both shins and palate, no new ones that I can see. No thrush. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. HIV off ART - same conversation; respect his choice today, door open. ID following.
2. Kaposi sarcoma - stable on exam; oncology following.
3. Prophylaxis - continue.
Physical in May.

documents.title: Refill Request - TMP-SMX
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request for TMP-SMX DS three times weekly; ID prescription ran out of refills. PCP sent 90-day supply with 1 refill. Patient notified.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

Working regularly with a framing crew this spring. Eating better. Still off ART; TMP-SMX MWF. Five years without cocaine or meth. Has a girlfriend now, sees her most weekends.

ROS: no fevers, cough, dyspnea, dysphagia, diarrhea, headaches. PHQ-9 4.

Exam: thin, well-appearing. Palate and shin plaques unchanged. No thrush. No nodes. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft, no HSM. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance - CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c. Colon screening due at 45 (2027). Flu in fall.
2. HIV off ART - asked again; he says "maybe after the summer." Safer sex reviewed.
3. Kaposi sarcoma - stable; oncology.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Timothy, labs look reasonable. Hemoglobin a bit better than last fall. Kidneys, liver, sugar and cholesterol fine.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL ED - PHYSICIAN NOTE (copy to PCP)
Arrival 8/20/2025 21:15

Brought in by his partner, who saw him have a generalized seizure at home. HIV, prior PJP, Kaposi sarcoma. He has been off antiretrovirals for more than a year, says because of side effects; has kept taking TMP-SMX prophylaxis.

Postictal on arrival, improving. No focal deficit documented on reassessment.

CD4 35/uL.
CT head: ring-enhancing lesion.

Impression: first seizure; ring-enhancing brain lesion in advanced HIV.

Disposition: loaded with levetiracetam; admitted to medicine with neurology and ID consultation.

documents.title: Call from Partner
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient's partner called (patient on speaker, gave verbal ok to talk with her). He had a seizure last night and is admitted at the regional hospital; they found something on the head CT and are doing more tests. Partner wanted us to know. PCP notified. Asked them to call when he is discharged so we can see him within the week.

conditions.label: Primary CNS lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell type (non-Hodgkin lymphoma)

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT

Here with his partner. Hospitalized 8/20 to 9/5. We have only the ED note; the rest is their account plus the discharge medication sheet he brought.

After the seizure the CT showed a lesion; MRI with contrast showed one enhancing spot. Toxoplasma blood test was negative (he had been taking his TMP-SMX). He had a needle biopsy through the skull on 8/29: lymphoma of the brain, large B-cell type. Oncology started chemotherapy in the hospital - high-dose methotrexate based, given every 2 weeks as an inpatient. Neurology started levetiracetam. On a dexamethasone taper. ART restarted in hospital, and this time he says he means it: "I don't want to die from this."

No seizures since. Mild headache the first week, gone. Tired after chemo.

Meds (discharge sheet): bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily; TMP-SMX DS MWF; levetiracetam 500 mg BID; dexamethasone taper; fluconazole prn; acetaminophen prn. Chemotherapy given by oncology.

Exam: thin, alert, oriented. Speech normal. CN intact, strength and gait normal. Healed small scalp incision. Palate and shin plaques unchanged. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Primary CNS lymphoma (non-Hodgkin, diffuse large B-cell) - oncology leads; requested their notes.
2. Seizure - levetiracetam BID; no driving (he doesn't drive), no working at heights on the crew until cleared - he says he is out of work during treatment anyway.
3. HIV - ART restarted; ID follow-up scheduled.
4. Kaposi sarcoma - unchanged.
RTC 6-8 weeks; call with any seizure, confusion, fever.

documents.title: Oncology Progress Note
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY - PROGRESS NOTE (copy to PCP, received by fax)

Diagnosis: primary CNS lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell type, solitary lesion, biopsy 8/29/2025; background HIV with CD4 35 at diagnosis.

Treatment: high-dose methotrexate-based induction, cycles every 14 days, given inpatient; tolerating with fatigue. Dexamethasone being tapered off.

Plan: continue induction; continue ART (restarted 9/2025), TMP-SMX prophylaxis and levetiracetam. Repeat brain MRI after induction.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Inactivated flu vaccine IM left deltoid; oncology ok'd timing between cycles. Afebrile. No seizures since discharge per patient. Tolerated well.

documents.title: Refill Request - Levetiracetam
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient down to 4 days of levetiracetam; hospital prescription had no refills. PCP sent levetiracetam 500 mg BID, 90-day supply. Pharmacy confirmed it will be ready this afternoon. He says chemo is going ok, "two more rounds."

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing better than I expected. Induction chemo almost done - last cycle scheduled for January, then oncology repeats the MRI. Off dexamethasone. No seizures on levetiracetam. Taking ART every day since September, organizer at his partner's place, and TMP-SMX MWF. ID saw him in November.

Tired after chemo weeks. Eating well; weight 64.

Exam: thin, alert. Speech and gait normal. Mouth: no thrush; palatal plaque unchanged. Shin plaques unchanged. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Primary CNS lymphoma - finishing induction with oncology.
2. Seizure - none since August; continue levetiracetam.
3. HIV - adherent since September. Proud of him; told him so.
4. Kaposi sarcoma - stable.
5. CBC and CMP today (chemo and TMP-SMX).
RTC after the January MRI, about 2-3 months.

documents.title: Labs from Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Timothy - hemoglobin is around 11, expected with chemo. Kidney and liver tests are ok for the next methotrexate cycle; I've sent a copy to oncology. Happy holidays.

documents.title: Refill Authorization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for TMP-SMX DS three times weekly. Last PCP fill 3/2025; ID now prescribing per pharmacy profile, but no refills left. Authorized 90 days. Patient's follow-up visit after the January MRI not yet booked - message left asking him to call.

documents.title: letter for housing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hi its Tim. the housing place says i need a letter from my doctor that i have medical conditions so i can get on the priority list for an apartment. can you do that

documents.title: Letter of Medical Necessity - Housing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the housing review committee:

Timothy Cole has been a patient of this practice since 2019. He has serious chronic medical conditions that require frequent appointments with several specialists, daily medications, and treatment that leaves him vulnerable to infection. Stable, private housing with reliable access to a refrigerator, a bathroom and a phone is medically important for him. I support his application for priority placement.

Please contact our office with questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: RE: letter for housing
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Tim, your letter is ready - signed copy at the front desk and a PDF attached here. Please also call to book your follow-up visit with the doctor; it's overdue.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL ED - PHYSICIAN NOTE (copy to PCP)
Arrival 5/1/2026 16:30

43M with HIV, prior PJP and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Six days of large-volume watery diarrhea with cramping and fatigue. No blood or mucus. Down 4 kg (9 lb) in a week. Ate raw vegetables at an outdoor picnic recently. No travel abroad, no recent antibiotics. Drinks bottled water at home. Reports he stopped his antiretrovirals a few months ago.

T 38.0 C. Mildly dry. Abdomen soft and nontender.

Stool modified acid-fast stain: round oocysts, 4-6 microns.

Impression: cryptosporidiosis with mild dehydration in advanced HIV.

Plan: IV fluids, oral rehydration and supportive care; antiretroviral therapy restarted; ID follow-up arranged. Discharged home. PCP follow-up advised.

documents.title: ED Note Received - Outreach
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PCP reviewed ED note from 5/1 (cryptosporidiosis, ART restarted) and asked that he be seen. Called patient's cell, voicemail; left message with our number asking him to book a visit. Portal message sent as well.
